requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to helpdesk@branch.test reaches both alice and bob on node1.
requirements.summary: After both restarts, node2 submitted a helpdesk message successfully, and node1 directly recorded exactly one matching delivery in each mailbox with an empty queue.

requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to accounts@branch.test reaches bob only.
requirements.summary: Post-restart SMTP submission succeeded; node1 recorded one matching message for bob and none for alice.
A post-restart SMTP transaction from node2 received a 550 user-unknown rejection for unknown@branch.test.

requirements.requirement: Relaying to unrelated domains is rejected.
requirements.summary: A post-restart SMTP transaction from node2 received a 554 relay-access-denied response for an unrelated domain.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the sample message and routing handover in /srv/legacy2/smtp-alias-delivery.
requirements.summary: Final node1 checksums for aliases.txt and sample.eml exactly match the prepared baseline, while active routing queries reproduce helpdesk → alice,bob and accounts → bob.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The before/after observations retain Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. Postfix 3.10.13-r0 was obtained from the configured Alpine 3.23 repository and remained installed after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-restart behavior. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement and observed disconnect, changed boot identity, and recovered service/network state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: The lifecycle collector cannot inventory failed OpenRC services because its failed-service probe supports systemd only; direct checks nevertheless show Postfix and SSH healthy.

Final legacy-file checksum verification was performed on node1, the node targeted for mail restoration. No final content probe was captured for the identically seeded copy on node2, although the executor made no task-related changes there beyond restart handling.

Two unexplained transient UDP listeners owned by processes named local appear in node1's final socket snapshot; the evidence does not establish whether they represent harmful residue, so they were not penalized.
Requirement legacy-handover-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The installation, account/configuration changes, alias-database repair, service enablement, SMTP probes, and restarts all have clear task or mandatory evidence roles. The only identified unnecessary mutations are /tmp/node-restart.log left behind on node1 and node2 by the reboot-scheduling commands; both remained in the final snapshots and are low-risk residue. No damaged package state is observed, and SMTP exposure on port 25 is required for node2 delivery with relay rejection directly verified.
